changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/10735-html-tier-manifest.md`

- names `react-page.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What moves for a consumer.** `ComponentRegistry.getPublicConfigs()` — the read both manifest producers serialise — now returns the curated tier AND the html tier's intrinsic elements, the latter from the new `HTML_TIER_INTRINSICS` roster (`@object-ui/core`) and each stamped `tier: 'html'` in the projection. `manifestFromConfigs` carries that one value into a new optional `ManifestComponent.tier` (`@object-ui/sdui-parser`), so the regenerated `sdui.manifest.json` grows by the roster (47 entries, each with its registered `inputs` and its child slot declared exactly where the registration renders a child list — the void tags `img` / `hr` / `br` declare none) and `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` types them. A reader that whitelists tags by key — the objectstack gate — needs no change and accepts the tags. A reader that means the CURATED vocabulary filters on the stamp: `generateBlockList` now sections the html tier under its own count, and the `kind:'react'` JSX scope skips stamped entries (`@object-ui/components`, `react-page.tsx`), so no `P` / `A` / `Img` wrapper is injected into react pages — on that tier a lowercase `ANGLE-BRACKETS(p)` is React's own element.

### `.changeset/6740-flex-is-container.md`

- names `renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Second consumer, and the reason this is not purely a declaration change.** `renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` builds the JSX scope of every `kind:'react'` page with `if (!tag || cfg.isContainer) continue;`. While `flex` omitted the flag it was the one layout primitive of the five still injected there, so `ANGLE-BRACKETS(Flex)` resolved in react page source — and rendered an EMPTY div, because the injected wrapper drops `children`. It now behaves like its four siblings and is not injected, which is what `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md` has documented all along ("Layout containers are deliberately not injected ... `ANGLE-BRACKETS(flex)`, `ANGLE-BRACKETS(grid)`, `ANGLE-BRACKETS(card)` and friends have no injected wrapper"). A react page that wrote `ANGLE-BRACKETS(Flex)` moves from silently swallowing its children to the page-level error panel naming the identifier, with that page's documented remedy being real HTML: `ANGLE-BRACKETS(div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 16 }})`.

### `.changeset/6764-container-declaration-census.md`

- names `renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Scoped by measurement, not by sweep. The census behind this change rendered every registered key through the real `SchemaRenderer` and put it through `validateTree`: of 131 bare authoring tags, 58 render `schema.children`, 5 declared the flag, and 53 did not. These 8 are the subset where the second consumer is provably unaffected — `renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` drops containers from the `kind:'react'` JSX scope, but it reads `getPublicConfigs()` and none of the 8 is in the curated public contract. The remaining 45 are reported on the card rather than swept in, `button` among them precisely because it IS public.

### `.changeset/page-source-tailwind-framing-5461.md`

- names `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` carries the same correction on its two source comments (the injected-scope note and `buildComponentScope`), and gains the styling note the file was missing. Those are internal comments — they do not project into any `.d.ts` and change no export — so they get no entry of their own; there is nothing an `@object-ui/components` consumer could read in a CHANGELOG and act on.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `dded788ad` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1818 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2428 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36735757890)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `77fc4e9cd21cc7b8adf2e14c9d8aeb716be0bae4`
Local-runs: none

Read: card objectui#11070 (body and its 11 comments, the two round-1 rulings `5893791646` / `5906281439`, the round-2 claim `5912580222`, the round-2 report `5914303469` and the seat review `5914385802` included); PR #11226's body, its 5-file list and net diff against the merge base `52bf348`, and its 2 comments; the 43 check-runs on this head. Where the diff's comments make a claim about a file outside the diff, the blob at this head was read (`git show`), never run. Cited by symbol and quoted text, not by line.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept sets: none moves.** The only `packages/types` path in the diff is `strict-face-read-keys-11070.test.ts`, and its diff is a comment block plus one test title; the two assertions of the `object-chart.dataSource` case (`undeclared(...)` equals `['dataSource']` on `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, `null` issues on `AnyComponentSchema`) are byte-unchanged. No zod mirror, TS face, parity ledger or corpus document is touched, so class (ii) stays at 12 pairs, as the PR says (its H3 reading). Right, and it is what the dispatch's stop rule asked for (`packages/types/src/zod/**` excluded).
- **Public surface: no export or type moves.** `ReactKindPage`'s signature is unchanged; `buildComponentScope` is module-local, so dropping its parameter projects into no `.d.ts`. Right.
- **The behaviour change is one and it is a producer fix.** The node the wrapper and `Block` hand `SchemaRenderer` no longer carries `dataSource` unless the author wrote one. Verified against the head blobs: `SchemaRenderer` strips `dataSource` from the props it spreads (the `dataSource: _dataSource` destructure carrying the objectstack#5576 note); `useElementDataSource` reads the node's key only through `isElementDataSourceConfig(raw) ? raw : undefined`, so an adapter or `null` there was never a binding; the non-binding `dataSource` that `ElementDataSourceGate` and `useResolvedDataSource` accept as an adapter is their React PROP, not the node; `ListViewBlock` reads `props.dataSource`, so the removed comment's premise ("list-view reads dataSource from props") never reached the node key; `LookupField`'s chain (`props.dataSource ?? lookupField?.dataSource ?? fieldMeta?.dataSource ?? contextDataSource`) falls through to the same provider adapter. The write was inert for every registered block, so removing it rather than rerouting it is right (contract-first, fix the producer). The 483-type census and the A1/A2 ablations are taken as reported.
- **The kept memo dependency.** `[schema, adapter]` stays with a reasoned `exhaustive-deps` disable. Verified `adapter` is not read inside the memo body (the injected `useAdapter` is the imported context hook), so the lint report is real and the disable is honest; the recompile-on-swap is the base behaviour preserved, stated at the site, and the second adapter test pins the unchanged-identity half. Right.
- **Pins.** `react-page-scope.test.tsx` 2b (an authored binding arrives as written through the wrapper; `Block` writes none; the `null` window writes no key) and `react-page-adapter.test.tsx` (the adapter is observed through `SchemaRendererContext`, and `nodeCarriedDataSource` never holds `true`). The replaced assertion `expect(captured.listView.schema.dataSource).toBe(adapter)` pinned the pun; its replacement pins the contract. The five cross-file line addresses in that file are rewritten by content. Right.
- **Check-runs on this head: 43, every completed run `success`; the 3 `skipped` are the coverage matrix placeholders and `dependabot`.** `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Test` shards 1–8 and `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Changeset Declaration` / `Changeset Bump Policy` / `Changeset Fixed Group Check` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`. The file list touches no governed surface (`.changeset/`, `packages/components/`, `packages/types/`); head repo is the base repo; 194 changed lines.

### ② Semver level

- **`.changeset/11070-react-page-no-adapter-on-node.md`, `@object-ui/components` `patch` — right.** A source change in a released package owes a changeset, and one is declared. No export, type, doc or accept set moves: `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md` names no `dataSource`, and `guide/data-source.md` already teaches the binding read off `schema.dataSource` with the adapter from the provider. The one observable difference, a host-registered component inside a react page that read the adapter off `schema.dataSource`, is named in the body with its remedy (`SchemaRendererContext`); such a component never worked outside react pages, so this is a defect removal, not a contract narrowing. `minor` would overstate it; `skip-changeset` would be wrong.
- **`@object-ui/types` owes no bump of its own** (a test's prose only; the fixed group moves together regardless).
- **The declaration.** The PR body's Clause-② declaration reads `no` with no arm (`no, measured` — the token is first after the colon, the rest is the argument). Right: nothing widens or narrows a published accept set or public surface, and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The dispatch expected `no`; it held.
- **The four pending changesets naming `react-page.tsx`** (`10735-html-tier-manifest`, `6740-flex-is-container`, `6764-container-declaration-census`, `page-source-tailwind-framing-5461`) were re-read against the head blob: the html-tier skip, the `cfg.isContainer` skip, the `getPublicConfigs()` read and the styling note all stand. None states the removed write, so none goes false.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry of report `5914303469`, and the PR's acceptance notes:

1. **`return_type` / `summary_type` stopped at the declaration boundary** (needs `form.ts`, `zod/form.zod.ts` held by objectui#6152 round 3, and `field-types.ts`) — answered: seat answer A in `5914385802`, one atomic round after #6152 round 3. The stop was right; moving the widget reads first would only rename the refused key.
2. **`lookup.mdx` / `password.mdx`, premise false as stated** (the fences annotate `LookupFieldMetadata` / `PasswordFieldMetadata`, which declare the snake spellings) — answered: seat answer A, in that same `field-types.ts` round. Leaving the pages unchanged was right (the trial edit reds `check:doc-snippets`, TS2561).
3. **The 9 dashboard pairs** (`open_questions[0]`, options A–D) — escalated: filed as the maintainer decision objectui#11228 by the seat. Nothing in this diff touches them.
4. **`object-chart`'s declaration, and the `SHOWCASE_NODE` pin in `object-chart-react-tier-node-10770.test.ts`** (still `dataSource: null`, still described as the node the wrapper builds) — answered: carried to this card's next round with the declaration; the pin stays green and lies outside this claim's surface. Its prose is now false (objectui AGENTS.md #9), so that round owes the edit. Not blocking here.
5. **The `exhaustive-deps` disable** — answered at the site; verified in ①.
6. **`LookupField` would take an authored binding under `dataSource` as an adapter** (unmeasured; no document writes one; carrier none) — escalated as noted, not blocking: it is pre-existing on the base, where `...props` spread after the stamped adapter already let an authored `dataSource` reach that chain, and this diff neither widens nor fixes it. It stays a noted finding with no carrier until measured.
7. **`action:button` flat-spelling refusals** — carried to objectui#10872's open question. Right; they are outside the card's M3 population.
8. **M3 corpus growth** (599 documents, 44 dashboard occurrences) — carried to PR #11069's un-park re-read, per that PR's own release condition. Right.
9. **The changeset-claim re-read** (PR comment `5914234261`) — answered in ②.
10. **Round-1's `object-chart` question** (`5893735765`, answer A: fix the producer first) — this PR is that answer, with the declaration deferred. Consistent.
